# hi

> hi is a single-binary CLI for Hifin machines and projects: it rents remote GPUs
> (Google Colab, Hugging Face Jobs, RunPod, Shadeform) with `hi compute`, starts
> projects from templates with `hi init`, sets up Ubuntu workstations with
> `hi install`, turns plain-words requests into shell commands with `hi q`,
> downloads the team's private Hugging Face data through a hi server with
> `hi data`, and puts a local service on a temporary public address with
> `hi net expose`. These notes are for coding agents such as Codex and Claude Code.

## Instructions for agents

1. Check whether hi is installed: `hi version`. If it is not, install the CLI
   only (no sudo, no system changes) with
   `curl -fsSL https://hifin.sh/install.sh | sh`; the binary lands in
   `~/.local/bin/hi`.
2. Load the hi skill, which matches the installed version and holds the rules
   you must follow. Print it with `hi skill --print`. To keep it for later
   sessions, ask the user before running `hi skill add hi --global` (every
   project) or `hi skill add hi` (this folder only).
3. Follow the skill rather than this page. The short version of its rules:
   ask before starting paid hardware and show the `--dry-run` plan first;
   always set `--max`; stop what you start and check `hi compute ls`; pass
   credentials with `--secret`, never `--env`; never approve your own requests
   on a hi server; and ask before `hi install`, `hi adduser`, `hi net`, or
   `hi update`, which change the machine. Get the team's data with `hi data`,
   never with a Hugging Face token of your own. Ask before `hi net expose`,
   keep its password, never use `--public` without the user's yes, and stop
   it when done.
4. Run `hi help`, `hi compute help`, or `hi init --help` for the exact options.

## Guide

- [Your first remote GPU](https://hifin.sh/guide/quickstart/): sign in, run a script, stop it
- [Let your coding agent use a GPU](https://hifin.sh/guide/examples/agent/): what to ask an agent, and what it does
- [Skills](https://hifin.sh/guide/reference/skill/): `hi skill` finds, installs, and updates agent skills from skills.sh, and writes the hi skill
- [All commands](https://hifin.sh/guide/reference/commands/): every command and option
- [Hand tasks to agents](https://hifin.sh/guide/agent/): `hi agent`, Claude Code, Codex, or Hermes on a task in a box, without permission prompts, with one report for every agent, and `--bundle web,office,data` for skills and the tools they need
- [Run code in a box](https://hifin.sh/guide/box/): `hi box`, a shell or a command in a rootless container with no credentials and a limited network, set up per project in `devcontainer.json` (`customizations.hi`, including `bundles`)
- [Share a local service](https://hifin.sh/guide/workstation/expose/): `hi net expose <port>`, a temporary public address for a service on this machine; ask the user first
- [Download the team's data](https://hifin.sh/guide/data/): `hi data`, the team's private Hugging Face datasets, models, and buckets through the hi server, on laptops, in boxes, in cloud jobs (`hi compute run --data`), and on machines you SSH into (`hi compute up --data`)
- [Ask for a command](https://hifin.sh/guide/q/): `hi q`, for people at a terminal; agents don't need it
- [Start a project](https://hifin.sh/guide/projects/): `hi init` templates, `--update`, and `--adopt`
- [Troubleshooting](https://hifin.sh/guide/reference/troubleshooting/): messages and what to do

## Optional

- [Install hi](https://hifin.sh/guide/install/): installer options and updating
- [Managed compute for a team](https://hifin.sh/guide/compute/managed/): requests and approvals through a hi server
- [Source](https://github.com/hifinab/cli)
